title: ARTEX source-qualified fingerprint review

review_annotations.preserve: Source-present User-Agent in the existing pinned BaaRai/reference artifacts.
review_annotations.annotation: At BaaRai commit 81eab87d166dddfc0d8be2707eadec788b61be0d, inspection of all 379 tracked Go blobs found ProbeSite/ResolveDomain only in interface declarations, method definitions and comments. ToolSet.SetEnrich stores the engine interface; worker wiring and engine construction do not establish invocation. No static call site was found. Treat the UA as implemented/source-present capability, not established runtime target egress.
review_annotations.limit: This is a source-level negative call-site result, not a native runtime callgraph or proof about modified/future code.

review_annotations.indicator: GET; artex-enrich/1.0; response read cap 1048576 bytes; no redirect follow
review_annotations.preserve: Prior native/static request-construction, literal, cap and redirect evidence.
review_annotations.annotation: Implemented request behavior and native function presence remain valid static findings. The same pinned source has no static ProbeSite/ResolveDomain call site. Neither finding proves a runtime request or an effective target-side detection rule. This review did not execute the v0.5.1 binary or establish a native runtime call graph.

Version-, lineage- and configuration-dependent. RuoJi6/ARTEX introduced the optional realm in 04c8c54ff8ba3d483094bef6f72e4e8ed8ff29b4. On 2026-11-03, 520317636467fe9a45052b7f1ebdcf8f0805924f replaced ARTEX with generic Restricted and removed service/version from health output. f053931a1df57916d5132a42f8920adf2f9aa842 then put health checks behind optional Basic Auth. Other forks can retain the old realm. Absence is inconclusive; Restricted is not a replacement ARTEX IOC. Chronology does not establish an evasion motive.
